name: Sweden
summary: Children are guaranteed half of their intestate share, and a spouse a minimum of four price base amounts. A foreign resident can choose the law of their nationality (EU Succession Regulation art. 22). Sweden has no trusts; private foundations are allowed but taxed.
reserved_share: Children and grandchildren: half of their intestate share (laglott), claim within six months of receiving the will. A surviving spouse can claim four price base amounts (Social Insurance Code ch. 2 ss. 6-7), as far as the estate allows.
foreign_law_note: EU Succession Regulation: the law of the last habitual residence applies by default (art. 21), but a resident foreign national may choose the law of their nationality (art. 22).
trust_note: Sweden is not in the HCCH table for the 1985 Trusts Convention. There is no Swedish trust; the tax agency taxes foreign trusts and foundations. Foundations (stiftelser, Foundations Act 1994:1220) may pursue any lawful purpose, including family ones, but only public-benefit ones are tax-exempt.
open_questions: The Swedish tax treatment of private foundations and foreign trusts was not sourced (a Bloomberg Tax headline only).
The ability to set up purely family foundations rests on a Philea summary and general commentary, not on the Act.
